title: Talent Profile
description: Profile of an influencer/creator for the NATIV2 AI marketing assistant. One file per talent (multi-talent roster).

$schema.description: Optional reference to this schema for IDE validation.

agency_id.description: Multi-tenant scope: FK to agency_profile.agency_id. Optional in v0.1 (single-tenant deploys may omit); required in v2 SaaS. When present, all cross-record queries MUST filter by agency_id to prevent cross-tenant data leakage. See docs/data_lineage.md GAP-01/02 for rationale.

id.description: Stable kebab-case slug, e.g. 'jane-doe'. Used as the primary key across phases. UNIQUENESS SCOPE: v0.1 globally unique (single tenant); v2 agency-scoped via composite UNIQUE `(agency_id, talent.id)` constraint — two agencies may both have `riley-carter`. See docs/id_conventions.md § 4 + GAP-N3.

content_niches.description: Primary content categories. Each value MUST be an `id` from `data/niches.json` (kebab-case slug, e.g. 'fitness', 'skincare', 'pc-gaming').

billing_entity.description: Legal/tax info needed to invoice brands. Used as the FROM party on every Phase 4.8 invoice generated for deals involving this talent. Distinguished from `agency_profile.billing_entity` which is the agency's own legal entity (used for outreach signature CAN-SPAM compliance, not invoicing). Whether the agency invoices on the talent's behalf or the talent invoices directly is governed by the `commission_split` model on `agency_profile.default_commission_model` + per-talent overrides via `talent.commission_override`.

commission_override.description: Per-talent override of agency-default commission terms. When absent, deals for this talent use `agency_profile.default_commission_rate` + `default_commission_model`. When present, these values take precedence. Captured in Phase 1 onboarding Step 5 (typically) or 7.5.

commission_rate.description: Decimal — 0.20 = 20% agency commission. Per-talent override of `agency_profile.default_commission_rate`.

commission_model.description: How money flows for this talent's deals. agency_invoices_brand_pays_talent_net: agency invoices brand for full fee; agency receives payment; agency pays talent (fee × (1-commission_rate)) net. talent_invoices_brand_agency_invoices_talent: talent invoices brand directly + agency separately invoices talent for commission. talent_invoices_brand_talent_pays_agency: talent invoices brand + manually pays agency commission. v0.1 Phase 4.8 invoicing uses the configured model to determine FROM-party on the brand-facing invoice + whether a sibling commission invoice is auto-generated.

invoice_payment_override.description: Per-talent override of agency-wide invoice payment instructions. When the talent's deals route payment to a different account than the agency's default, capture here. Renders into the `payment_instructions` block of invoices for this talent's deals (replaces `agency_profile.invoice_template.payment_instructions_markdown` for those invoices). Captured in Phase 1 onboarding Step 5.

payment_instructions_markdown.description: Bank details / IBAN / SWIFT / Stripe link / PayPal address. Supports merge fields (e.g. `{{invoice_number}}` as bank reference).

platforms.description: One entry per social platform the talent is active on.

audience_demographics.description: Aggregate audience demographics across all platforms. Per-platform overrides live on each platform entry.

age_bands.description: Share by age band as a percentage 0–100. Keys MUST be IAB Audience Taxonomy 1.1 Age Range bands so demographics bridge cleanly to industry audience profiles. IAB has no under-18 segment; if your platform analytics report under-18 share, exclude it from these percentages (re-normalise to 100% over 18+).

previous_brands.description: Brands the talent has worked with previously.

similar_talent.description: Other creators in the same competitive set — used for positioning and brand discovery.

rate_card.description: Price per deliverable, keyed by platform → deliverable type.

uplifts.description: Percentage uplifts on base price for extra rights.

preferred_industries.description: Industry IDs from `data/industries.json` the talent actively wants to work with.

blocked_industries.description: Industry IDs from `data/industries.json` the talent will not work with.

values_red_lines.description: Free-form hard nos beyond industry-level blocks (e.g. 'diet culture messaging').

industry_id.description: Industry the talent is exclusive in. Must match an `id` in `data/industries.json`.

brand.description: The brand the exclusivity is with.

contract_template.description: Per-talent contract template used by the Phase 4.7 contract pack generator (`docs/contract_pack_workflow.md`). Captured during Phase 1 talent onboarding. Markdown source with `{{merge_field}}` placeholders, `{{#if condition}}...{{/if}}` conditional sections, and `{{narrative_*}}` LLM-drafted blocks. Party identification (legal entity name, country, tax ID, address) is pulled from `talent.billing_entity` — single source of truth. Working defaults (usage rights, turnaround, revisions) are pulled from `talent.working_terms`. Agencies can ship starter templates in `data/contract_template_starters/` that the onboarding flow copies into this field for editing.

markdown_source.description: The full contract template text in markdown. Contains `{{merge_field}}` for deterministic substitution, `{{#if condition}}...{{/if}}` for conditional clauses (closes with matching `{{/if}}`), and `{{narrative_*}}` for LLM-drafted sections. The renderer composes this markdown source after merge/condition/narrative passes and emits .md (source-of-truth), .docx (via python-docx), .pdf (via Puppeteer or pandoc).

merge_field_definitions.description: Every merge field the template uses, with its expected source. Drives Stage B (merge field extraction) — LLM knows where to pull each value from and can flag low-confidence extractions for agent review.

source.description: Where the value comes from. `agent_input` = agent must provide (typically brand legal entity info). `computed` = derived from other fields (e.g. signed_date = today).

source_path.description: Dotted path within the source (e.g. 'billing_entity.legal_name', 'proposal.fee_usd'). Optional — omit for free-text fields the agent fills.

required.description: If true, draft contract cannot pass legal review until value is set. Critical fields (legal names, fees, dates) should be required.

default.description: Fallback value if source extraction fails or returns null.

description.description: Human-readable explanation for the agent reviewing in UI.

clause_applicability_rules.description: Per-conditional-block rule that determines whether the clause fires. Evaluated in Stage C. Each rule has a human-readable description (for agent + audit) AND a structured condition (machine-evaluatable). The LLM evaluates the condition against full deal/proposal/debrief context and decides include/exclude with rationale.

clause_id.description: Matches the `{{#if clause_id}}` identifier in markdown_source.

description.description: What this clause covers (e.g. 'EU GDPR data-processing addendum').

condition.description: Plain-language condition the LLM evaluates (e.g. 'brand registered address is in the EU', 'deal.proposal.exclusivity.duration_days > 0'). Structured JSONLogic could replace this in v0.2 for deterministic evaluation; v0.1 lets the LLM interpret natural-language conditions for flexibility.

default_decision.description: If `include` / `exclude`, decision is fixed — LLM doesn't evaluate. `llm_decide` runs Stage C evaluation.

applicability_source.description: Hint to LLM about which context block to inspect.

narrative_placeholders.description: Sections the LLM drafts (Stage D). Each placeholder names what context to draw from + tone guidance.

draws_from.description: List of context sources to draw from (e.g. ['deal.proposal.deliverables', 'discovery_debrief.objectives_heard']).

tone.description: Tone guidance (e.g. 'formal legal prose, no marketing language').

default_governing_law.description: Default governing-law jurisdiction (e.g. 'England and Wales', 'State of California, USA'). Used as merge field default if not overridden per deal.

legal_reviewer_id.description: Optional. If set, only this identity can pass the hard legal review gate (e.g. external legal counsel). Defaults to the deal's assigned_agent_id if absent. The reviewer's identity is captured in `contract_pack.legal_review.approved_by_agent_id` on gate-pass.

template_version.description: Semver or freeform version label. Updated whenever markdown_source / merge_field_definitions / clause_applicability_rules / narrative_placeholders / default_governing_law / default_jurisdiction change. Captured in `contract_pack.context_snapshot.template_version_used` for traceability — if a template changes mid-deal, prior contract packs stay anchored to the version they were generated from. ENFORCEMENT (GAP-08): API layer MUST bump this string + set template_updated_at on every modification to those fields. Version bump is a DB-enforced trigger or a service-layer guard — never trust manual update. Critical for legal audit trail: a signed contract's clause set must always be reproducible from the captured template_version.

based_on_starter_template_id.description: If the template was adopted from one of the agency's starter templates (`data/contract_template_starters/`), the starter's ID is captured here. Provenance — easier to track which talent templates have diverged from which starters.

other_stats.description: Free-form key/value bag for anything that doesn't fit (newsletter subs, Discord size, podcast downloads, etc.).

primary.description: True if this is the talent's main platform.

audience_demographics_override.description: Optional per-platform override of the top-level audience_demographics.

api_credentials.description: References to credentials — never the raw secret.

brandDeal.description: Light index entry for a past brand campaign. The full rich record (KPIs, vs-benchmark, audience-overlap, re-engagement metadata, etc.) lives in `data/brand_deals/{talent_id}.json`. Optional `deal_id` field links the two — when present, the orchestrator reads the rich record from there. Kept in talent.json for backwards compatibility + fast scans without loading the deals file.

industry_id.description: Industry ID from `data/industries.json`. The app auto-suggests this from `brand` via `data/brand_industry_map.json` (exact + alias + domain match) and falls back to AI inference.

deal_id.description: Optional FK to a rich deal record in `data/brand_deals/{talent_id}.json`. When set, the rich KPIs, vs-benchmark performance, audience-overlap, and re-engagement metadata are sourced from there. When absent (legacy or skeleton entries), the orchestrator falls back to the inline fields below.

similarTalent.description: Thin pointer to a competitor/comparable creator. Starts as a seed (name + handles) and is enriched by AI research over time. `previous_brands` is the source of truth; `inferred_niches` is back-derived from those brands by inverting `data/niche_industry_affinity.json` (industry -> niches that resonate).

handles.description: Public platform handles. Starting point for AI research.

previous_brands.description: Known brand collaborations. Each `industry_id` is auto-resolved via `data/brand_industry_map.json` (or AI inference fallback). This list is the source of truth — niches are derived from it, not authored.

industry_id.description: Industry ID from `data/industries.json`. Optional on input — resolved by the app from the brand name.

source.description: Where this collaboration was observed (URL, post handle, manual entry).

inferred_niches.description: Niches back-derived from `previous_brands` by inverting `data/niche_industry_affinity.json` — for each industry, which niches list it as a primary/secondary/tertiary match? Computed by the app, not hand-authored. Stored on the record so it persists between sessions and can be reviewed/overridden.

confidence.description: Aggregated strength across all this creator's previous brands. `primary` if multiple brands point at this niche at primary tier; weaker otherwise.

supporting_brands.description: The previous_brands entries (by brand name) that contributed to this inference.

research.description: AI-research workflow metadata. Tracks enrichment state so the app knows when to refresh.

status.description: `seed` = name+handles only; `researching` = AI run in flight; `enriched` = previous_brands + inferred_niches populated; `failed` = AI couldn't enrich; `stale` = enriched but past refresh window.

sources.description: URLs / source notes the AI used to enrich this record.

nicheId.description: Kebab-case slug that MUST match an `id` in `data/niches.json`. Pattern-validated here; semantic match enforced at load time by the app.

industryId.description: Kebab-case slug that MUST match an `id` in `data/industries.json`. Pattern-validated here; semantic match enforced at load time by the app.
